references.text: The disciples had gone into the town to buy food (John 4:8), and now that they are back, they urge Jesus to eat. This is the narrative context for their request.
The title "Rabbi" is also used for Jesus in John 1:38, where the disciples address him with this honorific meaning "teacher" for the first time.
Nicodemus calls Jesus "Rabbi" in John 3:2, showing that even outsiders recognized Jesus as a teacher.
John's disciples call Jesus "Rabbi" in John 3:26, confirming that this was a common form of address used for Jesus.
Jesus' answer in John 4:32–34 reveals that he has food deeper than the physical food the disciples offer him—namely, to do the will of the Father and complete his work.

During the temptation in the wilderness, Jesus fasted for forty days and declared that man does not live by bread alone (Matthew 4:2–4). This shows that Jesus prioritized spiritual nourishment over physical food, just as he does here.

In Deuteronomy 8:3, the Lord says that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord. Jesus lives out this principle when he deprioritizes physical food in favor of doing God's will.
In John 6:27, Jesus speaks about working for the food that lasts to eternal life, not the perishable food—a theme that also underlies this passage where the disciples urge him to eat.
